findings.reason: the plan must bind `nova/biot/null.py` to a destination (retire the mesh-flux quadratic null finder, or state it becomes the field representation `topology.read` evaluates) or the omission leaves a second null authority in place and the §6 retirement test cannot pass.
findings.text: the design's 17-file null inventory binds `_FixedDesignNull2D` (forward_operator.py), `critical_point_candidates_batch` (stencil_nulls.py) and the rest to `topology.read`, but never names `nova/biot/null.py` (`Null1D`/`Null2D`) or `nova/biot/fieldnull.py`, the field-null position/value kernels that the files it is replacing actually import (`topology.py:14` `from nova.biot.null import Null1D, Null2D`; `forward_operator.py:42` `from nova.biot.null import Null2D, inside_or_near_source_cell`). A retirement that cannot name the owner it retires leaves the old null authority importable, and §6's acceptance already requires `test_retired_routes_are_unreachable` to prove only `solve.fixed_point` survives — so the inventory has an unbound owner.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — each of the four proposed signatures hides a large body behind a smaller result. `topology.read` hides the contour-tree authority plus sub-cell axis-connected membership behind one `TopologyRead`; `solve.fixed_point` hides the verified ~590-line GMRES kernel and the line search behind one `SolveResult`. Verified in `nova/equilibrium/fixed_point.py`: `_active_set_newton_krylov` is 24 parameters over 591 lines and `newton_krylov` 30 parameters — the sprawl the plan collapses is real, and the plan replaces it with four functions rather than a fan of shallow wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the null-role retirement inventory that binds the 17 `nova/equilibrium` files omits the field-null owner `nova/biot/null.py` (`Null1D`/`Null2D`) and `nova/biot/fieldnull.py`, which `topology.py` and `forward_operator.py` import today and which §2's `topology.read` is positioned to supersede.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0 (read 2026-10-05T17:31:31Z). No section adds interface surface without naming what it retires in its own text: §2 names `Topology.read` and `read_with_connectivity`, §3 names `clipped_support_current_moments` and the `forward_operator.py` support partition, §4 names the `ForwardFluxOperator` map, §5 names `newton_krylov`/`picard`/`operator_request_body`, and §6 names the promotion/recovery, frozen/live, active-set, Anderson, reduced-Newton and chord paths as deleted — and the two new operand types (`TopologyPolicy`, `SolvePolicy`) are stated as carried by the existing `ForwardSolvePolicy` in `solve_request.py`, "extended rather than duplicated".
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan's design document carries a full source inventory binding 17 null-role files and 23 region-role files to a retirement destination each (design doc "Source inventory and retirement destinations"), and the plan's recorded reuse ruling (comment `c-20261005T171941782407`) names the existing single-site GMRES kernel in `nova/equilibrium/fixed_point.py` (`_single_site_krylov`, `_krylov_machine`, `_serve_krylov_stream`, `_krylov_outputs`, the Gram-Schmidt/least-squares helpers, ~590 lines, verified) and the Armijo `_steepest_descent_promotion` as reuse candidates for §5, so the plan cites the machinery it searched and what it keeps.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan states each module as a replacement in place, not a layer over the old one: "`gs.apply` replaces the map `ForwardFluxOperator` performs today rather than wrapping it" and "`topology.py` is replaced in place". The one thin adapter — `forward.py` shrinking to "the request and receipt adapter" — is justified in the design as the existing `ForwardSolveRequest → ForwardProfile.solve → ForwardSolveReceipt` host seam, which is the honest reason a thin layer survives here.
